candidate.title: TL-seq
candidate.scope: The assigned TL-seq middle row, labeled Enzymatic capture of m7G-capped mRNA 5′ ends: cap-selective short-RNA library architecture ending in cDNA. The direct 3′-adapter-ligation depiction is supported by the TL-seq biological-replicate implementation in Arribere and Gilbert (2013), within the broader TL-seq method. SMORE-Seq above, TATL-seq below, a clipped PEAT row at the top, and chemical structures at the right are neighboring context, with no connecting route into this card’s TL-seq workflow. The extra early reverse-transcription caption is retained as a source discrepancy and resolved from the primary paper.

operations.label: Fragmentation and size selection
operations.description: Break the starting mRNA into shorter RNA pieces and retain a size-selected population, including the capped 5′ fragment and fragments with other 5′ end groups.
operations.mechanism: The primary TL-seq preparation uses alkaline hydrolysis followed by fragment size selection.
operations.information_effect: The original transcript-start sequence survives in the cap-bearing terminal fragment; fragmentation removes continuity to the rest of the transcript.

Fragmented and size-selected RNA is first treated with a phosphatase, reducing the majority of 5′ RNA ends to hydroxyl groups, leaving m7G-capped 5′ ends intact.

operations.label: Phosphatase
operations.description: Convert exposed phosphorylated 5′ ends to hydroxyl ends while the m7G-capped 5′ end is protected.
operations.mechanism: Calf-intestinal phosphatase (CIP) in the primary preparation; the diagram depicts GPPP unchanged and the other 5′ groups as OH.
operations.information_effect: Creates a chemical distinction between cap-protected transcript ends and uncapped background fragments in the same pool.

evidence.quote: Fragmented and size-selected RNA is first treated with a phosphatase, reducing the majority of 5′ RNA ends to hydroxyl groups, leaving m7G-capped 5′ ends intact.
calf-intestinal phosphatase (CIP; NEB)

operations.label: Pyrophosphatase
operations.description: Remove the cap from the protected RNA end to expose a 5′ monophosphate; previously dephosphorylated background ends remain hydroxylated.
operations.mechanism: Tobacco acid pyrophosphatase (TAP) is the primary implementation of the depicted pyrophosphatase step.
operations.information_effect: Converts cap history into selective ligatability; the cap is removed but its former location is retained as the ligatable RNA boundary.

operations.label: Ligate 5′ adapter
operations.description: Attach the supplied green RNA adapter to the 5′-monophosphate, formerly capped fragment; the diagram retains unligated OH fragments in the mixture.
operations.mechanism: RNA ligation selects the monophosphate substrate over the 5′-OH fragments; the primary preparation identifies T4 RNA ligase.
operations.information_effect: Physically tags the retained transcript-start fragment and creates a length shift for subsequent purification. Selectivity does not imply complete removal of biological background.

operations.label: Gel purify
operations.description: Select the higher-molecular-weight 5′-adapter-ligated RNA from the fragment pool. The primary paper resolves the diagram’s extra early Reverse transcription caption: RNA, rather than cDNA, is purified here.

operations.information_effect: Enriches the adapter-bearing formerly capped terminal fragments; untagged fragments are excluded from the retained route.

operations.label: Ligate 3′ adapter

checks.rationale: The independently inspected target is the middle TL-seq row. All 10 states, 7 local operations and 16 material connections have been individually checked against the image and relevant full text, including both sides of every interface. The cap-selection sequence, gel-retained RNA, direct 3′ adapter addition and final cDNA conversion are represented. The four end-group icons describe one mixed preparation, not separate experimental branches; the two adapter additions are genuine multi-input joining operations. No compartment, pooling or alternative route is depicted within the assigned row. The duplicate early RT caption is explicitly retained and resolved from the scoped primary implementation. Direct 3′ ligation is appropriately tied to TL-seq biological replicates, preserving its distinction from the original poly(A)-tailing preparation. Short terminal-fragment sequence in cDNA is the readout carrier, and non-TSS background is acknowledged. No consequential unsupported assertion or omitted in-scope transformation remains.
